## Appearance

Susan is a grim-faced, gaunt, and elderly spinster. She admits herself that she is no beauty.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v5 c17 P33](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0033), [v5 c30 P14](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0014)_

## Personality

Susan is a kind-hearted, pragmatic, and faithful woman who manages household duties with calm competence. Though practical and unsentimental in daily life, she possesses a romantic side and is open about her fondness for men despite never having had a suitor. She is fiercely protective and tender toward those in her care, particularly Shirley Blythe. She takes strong pride in her cooking and holds distinct, opinionated views on ears and manners.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c19 P41](../source/v04-c19.md#nw-v04-c19-p0041), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v4 c22 P5](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0005), [v4 c24 P7](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0007), [v4 c24 P9](../source/v04-c24.md#nw-v04-c24-p0009), [v4 c34 P17](../source/v04-c34.md#nw-v04-c34-p0017), [v4 c40 P49](../source/v04-c40.md#nw-v04-c40-p0049), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P4](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0004), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005), [v5 c26 P8](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0008), [v5 c26 P9](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0009), [v5 c30 P14](../source/v05-c30.md#nw-v05-c30-p0014)_

## History

Susan Baker, a spinster from Glen St. Mary, was installed as maid-of-all-work for Dr. Gilbert Blythe and Anne Shirley at their home at Four Winds. She took charge of household duties and cooking, taking great pride in her domestic work and remaining fiercely faithful to the family. When the Blythes relocated to Ingleside, Susan continued as their gray, grim, and devoted handmaiden. Following the birth of Shirley Blythe, when Anne was gravely ill, Susan mothered the infant with passionate tenderness, nursing him to health and treating him as her special favorite. Over the years, she managed the household, cooked meals, knitted clothes for neighbors, and actively took part in raising the Blythe children.

_Sources: [v4 c18 P52](../source/v04-c18.md#nw-v04-c18-p0052), [v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003), [v5 c1 P0](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0000), [v5 c1 P4](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0004), [v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005), [v5 c25 P4](../source/v05-c25.md#nw-v05-c25-p0004), [v5 c26 P8](../source/v05-c26.md#nw-v05-c26-p0008)_

> Susan is at the helm. There is no use in keeping a dog and doing your own barking.  <sub>[v4 c22 P3](../source/v04-c22.md#nw-v04-c22-p0003)</sub>

> I gave him life just as much as you did, Mrs. Dr. dear. He is just as much my baby as he is yours.  <sub>[v5 c1 P5](../source/v05-c01.md#nw-v05-c01-p0005)</sub>

> I am no beauty, Mrs. Dr. dear, and well I know it, and have always known it, but that I am as ugly as that picture makes me out I will never, no, never believe.  <sub>[v5 c17 P33](../source/v05-c17.md#nw-v05-c17-p0033)</sub>
